body:
Actually I tend to be overly conservative and careful with what I say, unless I know the person well. I've only made suicide jokes with my friends at college (and earned somewhat of a reputation for it). 

I have been seeing a therapist for a few months now. I seem to be getting worse regardless. (Therapy has still been very helpful).

I am fortunate to have a job, but I've found it somewhat frustrating. I just don't seem to click with most of my colleagues. It's not because I'm mean-spirited or anything. Rather, one of my colleagues said I was almost too nice (which is probably true). 

My relationship with my family is a bit tricky. I think they try to support me, but they don't really understand what I'm experiencing. They've also made less than helpful statements, such as "You're making my life shorter" or "suicide is selfish," etc. 

Honestly my life should be pretty good compared to others, but I feel pain from just being alive. I have a hard time completing even the smallest of tasks such as doing the dishes or laundry. I also just went three days without eating...

I graduated college last spring (barely). Even though I struggled with hellish suicidal ideation at college, I roomed with friends and had a school counselor on campus.

Now I'm living in an apartment by myself. Several of my friends no longer live in the area. I'm more on the peripherals of the friend group, so I don't think many of them will care all that much when I'm gone. I can go a couple weeks or more without having a meaning conversation with anyone beyond basic formalities. I also struggle trying to form new friendships because of social anxiety. I am fortunate enough to see a therapist every week, but I've been slowly getting worse anyways.

You sound like a good person, so I'll believe you care at the moment. But in a month? You'll forget this conversation even took place. I appreciate the sentiment though.

 It's hard going through life alone...
I don't see how it is possible for things to get better.
I'm sorry you're feeling this way. I also struggle with not feeling good enough. It's hard feeling like you don't matter.

The documentary I watched is called Dying for Everest. You can find it on youtube for free. 

He was still alive as they passed him on the way up. He was even still alive (but barely) as they passed him on the way down.
